title: Urban Mental Health – phase 1
summary:
Mental health issues can affect how well we feel and perform, and they are linked to shorter lifespans. These problems also put a strain on healthcare systems and contribute to high rates of absenteeism and early retirement.
Children and teenagers, especially in urban areas, face an increased risk of mental health problems due to factors like poverty, migration, and pollution. 
The multi-level approach of the UMH project aims to improve mental health of kids in a specific area with many disadvantaged families.  Professionals working with children (teachers, kindergardeners, social workers and professionals in counselling centres) receive mental health training. Other interventions of UMH aim at improving working conditions, professional networks, and structural conditions in schools, kindergardens and counselling centres.
The project is evaluated in terms of children’s mental health, professionals’ mental health and mental health literacy, working conditions, professional networks, and structural conditions in schools, kindergardens and counselling centres. We also assess the success, acceptance, feasibility, and sustainability of each single intervention. Throughout, the research project representatives of all stakeholder groups (e.g., children, teachers etc.) are continuously involved.
